final_sql: SELECT Major, Age FROM Student WHERE StuID NOT IN (SELECT hp.StuID FROM Has_Pet hp JOIN Pets p ON hp.PetID = p.PetID WHERE p.PetType = 'cat' AND hp.StuID IS NOT NULL) LIMIT 100
answer:
33 of the 34 students don't have a cat. The only student with a cat is 1001 (Linda Smith), who has pet 2001. Here are the (Major, Age) pairs for the other 33:

| Major | Age |
|---|---|
| 600 | 19, 21, 20, 26, 18, 18, 20, 19, 17, 22, 20, 18, 16, 17, 27, 20, 18 |
| 520 | 22, 19, 20, 18, 19, 18 |
| 540 | 17, 18 |
| 550 | 20, 21, 20, 20, 18 |
| 100 | 17 |
| 50 | 18, 26 |

Assumptions:
- "Do not have a cat" includes students who have no pet at all, as well as students who only have other pets such as dogs.
- `Major` is stored as a numeric code, so the results show codes rather than major names. The database has no table that maps them to names.

The query was:

```sql
SELECT Major, Age FROM Student
WHERE StuID NOT IN (
  SELECT hp.StuID FROM Has_Pet hp
  JOIN Pets p ON hp.PetID = p.PetID
  WHERE p.PetType = 'cat' AND hp.StuID IS NOT NULL)
```
